challenges.headline: Edit vs. adjustment vs. override
challenges.premise: The request treats 'edit the total' as a direct change to the reported figure.
challenges.alternative: Recording the correction as a separate, attributed adjustment entry keeps the total reconciling back to its own source data — the override instead replaces the derived value and silently disagrees with the entries underneath it.
challenges.consequence: An override that isn't visibly flagged is how a report quietly stops tying out — the exact failure mode finance and auditors are least forgiving of.
challenges.recommendation: Confirm with Finance whether corrections must remain traceable to source entries before the data model is built.

challenges.headline: Editing after period close
challenges.premise: The request doesn't distinguish whether a total in a closed period can still be edited.
challenges.alternative: Routing post-close corrections through a next-period adjustment or a formal restatement keeps closed figures frozen and every downstream export or filing consistent with what was actually closed.
challenges.consequence: Allowing direct edits to closed-period figures invalidates anything already exported or filed from that period, and reconciling the difference later is expensive.
challenges.recommendation: Define the period-close rule (frozen vs. editable) with Finance before touching the edit workflow.

challenges.headline: Export as a one-off file
challenges.premise: The request frames export as 'sending figures to the finance team,' implying a simple file drop.
challenges.alternative: Treating the export as a versioned, retained artifact means what was sent stays reproducible even if the underlying figures are later corrected — a distinct file per send, not a live query.
challenges.consequence: Without versioning, a later correction makes it impossible to prove what was actually sent to finance on a given date, which is precisely what gets questioned at audit time.
challenges.recommendation: Clarify the export's format, rounding convention, and whether it must remain retrievable exactly as sent.
